description: The owner's real grz100 sheet (grz100.pdf, never committed; gated on RELAY_SAMPLE_PDF_DIR).

sources: BFR characteristic angle (fixed 75 deg to the R-axis)
right.equation: Rright(X) = BFRS + X * cot(75 deg); the forward blinder BFR: X >= (R - BFRS) * tan 75 deg (Toshiba 6F2S0834-0, 2.6.1, Fig. 2.6.1.9: 'The BFR has an angle of 75 deg to the R-axis'; 'The characteristic of the BFR is obtained by the following equation. X >= (R - Rs) tan 75 deg', Rs = BFRS, 'the reach setting'; settings p. 34, BFRS angle 'Fixed to 75 deg'). BFRS is one forward right blinder common to Z1, Z1X, Z2, ZF and Z3 on this sheet. The reverse zones' blinder (BRR/BRRS), ZND's blinder (BNDS), the left blinder BFL and the directional element are separately scoped and not represented by this boundary.

sources: BFL origin intercept (BFLS fixed at 0 ohm, no configurable reach)
left.equation: Rleft(X) = X * cot(BFLSθ); derived from Vp * I * cos(φ + θ - 90°) > 0 (6F2S0834-0, 2.6.1, Fig. 2.6.1.9, p.119-120) as sin(φ + θ) > 0, i.e. R * sin θ >= X * cos θ, i.e. R >= X * cot(BFLSθ), with BFLS fixed at 0 ohm (settings p.34: 'BFLS θ 90-135 deg ... 120 deg ... Forward left blinder angle'; BFLS intercept always at the origin). BFLSθ is the configured inclination angle of BFL to the R-axis (90-135 deg, default 120 deg, read from the sheet). Static equivalent: the relay uses cross-polarisation with voltage memory (Toshiba 6641-1); this boundary is the DC steady-state geometry. The reverse blinder BRL and the ZBS directional element are separately scoped and not represented by this boundary.
